The [[1968 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the X Olympic Winter Games, were an international winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Grenoble]], France, from 4 to 18 February 1968.<ref>{{cite web |title=1968 Winter Olympics Overview |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/38 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=17 March 2025 |archive-date=15 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715232551/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/38 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=FAQ: What are the Olympic Games? |url=http://olympic.ca/2019/02/08/faq-what-are-the-olympic-games/ |website=[[Canadian Olympic Committee]] |date=2019-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240805233326/http://olympic.ca/2019/02/08/faq-what-are-the-olympic-games/ |archive-date=2024-08-05 |url-status=live |access-date=20 February 2025}}</ref> A total of 1,158 athletes representing 37 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grenoble 1968 Winter Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240729060019/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968 |archive-date=29 July 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=6 August 2024 }}</ref> This included first-time entrant [[Morocco]],<ref>{{cite web |title=A brief history of African nations at the Winter Olympics |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/brief-history-african-nations-winter-olympics |website=[[NBC Olympics]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606100209/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/brief-history-african-nations-winter-olympics |archive-date=6 June 2023 |url-status=live |agency=[[Reuters]] |access-date=6 August 2024 |language=en }}</ref> as well as [[East Germany at the 1968 Winter Olympics|East]] and [[West Germany at the 1968 Winter Olympics|West Germany]], who entered separate teams for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |title=1968 Grenoble, France |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/1968-grenoble-france-1.851453 |website=[[CBC Sports]] |date=2009-12-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227163417/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/1968-grenoble-france-1.851453 |archive-date=2024-12-27 |url-status=live |access-date=25 September 2010}}</ref> The games featured 35 events in 6 [[Winter Olympic sports|sports]] and 10 disciplines,<ref name="Winter games fact sheet">{{Cite web |date=2024-06-20 |title=Factsheet – The Olympic Winter Games |url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240711124443/http://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-date=11 July 2024 |access-date=6 August 2024 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |page=4}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=1968 Winter Olympics Overview |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/38 |website=[[Olympedia]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715232551/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/38 |archive-date=15 July 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=6 August 2024 }}</ref> including the [[Biathlon at the 1968 Winter Olympics – Relay|team relay event]] in the [[Biathlon at the 1968 Winter Olympics|biathlon]], which was contested for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biathlon 101: Olympic history |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/biathlon-101-olympic-history |website=[[NBC Olympics]] |date=2021-10-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003143847/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/biathlon-101-olympic-history |archive-date=3 October 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=6 August 2024 |language=en }}</ref>

Athletes representing 15 NOCs won at least one medal, with 13 winning at least one gold medal.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> [[Norway at the 1968 Winter Olympics|Norway]] won the most medals overall, with 14, and the most gold medals, with 6.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> East and West Germany won their first Winter Olympic medals of any kind as independent teams,<ref name="East Germany Olympedia">{{cite web |title=East Germany (GDR) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/GDR |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=17 March 2025 |archive-date=13 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250213002420/https://www.olympedia.org/countries/GDR |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="West Germany Olympedia">{{cite web |title=West Germany (FRG) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/FRG |website=[[Olympedia]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250308094435/https://www.olympedia.org/countries/FRG |archive-date=8 March 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=17 March 2025 }}</ref> as did Romania,<ref name="Romania IOC">{{cite web |title=Romania – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/romania |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006044118/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/romania |archive-date=2024-10-06 |url-status=dead |access-date=March 17, 2025}}</ref> while East and West Germany, along with [[Czechoslovakia at the 1968 Winter Olympics|Czechoslovakia]], won their first Winter Olympic gold medals.<ref name="East Germany Olympedia" /><ref name="West Germany Olympedia" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=22 January 2012 |title=Jiri Raska, 1968 Olympic Ski Jumping Champion, Dies at 70 (Published 2012) |url=http://nytimes.com/2012/01/23/sports/skiing/jiri-raska-olympic-ski-jumping-champ-dies-at-70.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=17 March 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]] |language=en |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=21 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121012007/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/01/23/sports/skiing/jiri-raska-olympic-ski-jumping-champ-dies-at-70.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Among individual participants, French alpine skier [[Jean-Claude Killy]] won the most gold medals with three. Killy (three gold), Swedish cross-country skier [[Toini Gustafsson]] (two gold, one silver), and Finnish cross-country skier [[Eero Mäntyranta]] (one silver, two bronze) tied for the most medals overall, with three each.<ref>{{cite web |title=1968 Grenoble Winter Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1968/ |website=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=17 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417042444/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1968/ |archive-date=April 17, 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Medal table==
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by an NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] |date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>

At the 1968 Winter Games, in [[Speed skating at the 1968 Winter Olympics|speed skating]], two-way ties for second place in the [[Speed skating at the 1968 Winter Olympics – Men's 500 metres|men's 500]] and [[Speed skating at the 1968 Winter Olympics – Men's 1500 metres|1,500 metres]] events, as well as a three-way tie in the [[Speed skating at the 1968 Winter Olympics – Women's 500 metres|women's 500 metres]] event, resulted in the awarding of an additional four silver medals; as a consequence, three bronze medals were not awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grenoble 1968 500m men Results – Olympic speed-skating |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968/results/speed-skating/500m-men |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009081409/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968/results/speed-skating/500m-men |archive-date=9 October 2024 |access-date=17 March 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Grenoble 1968 1500m men Results – Olympic speed-skating |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968/results/speed-skating/1500m-men |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009081409/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968/results/speed-skating/1500m-men |archive-date=9 October 2024 |access-date=17 March 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Grenoble 1968 500m women Results – Olympic speed-skating |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968/results/speed-skating/500m-women |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119191534/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/grenoble-1968/results/speed-skating/500m-women |archive-date=19 January 2025 |access-date=17 March 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref>
